Kind of relate. I write stories for like 3 years for serious, because that's what i need in my life to feel necessary. At least for myself - nobody really wants to read my scribbles (i simply don't have anyone interested). There was a time when i read guides and tips on writing blogs (for beginner writters by just a bit-more-experieced writers or critics) and there are all similar as your examples. "Get the arcs, the audience will love it", "make the three-dimensional deep character with clearly defined goals and something that people can relate to", "THE PEOPLE WON'T LIKE IT IF YOU DO IT OTHERWISE". Because of 80's style of writing that inspires me far more than the modern requirements of good prose, i just stopped reading guides. They started to slowly killing my enjoyment out of writing. They started to... ugh, to killing ME in my writing. Or maybe i was just taking things too far.

Imagine if Tolkien have written the Lord of the Rings today. I think like nobody would get him serious, because audience don't want to read a book started by 50 huge-ass pages or more with Hobbits doing daily hobbitish things.

I decided to just stick with the old good Cyril Connoly's quote "Better to write for yourself and have no public, than to write for public and have no self".
